question: The contraction and relaxation of which of the following results in movement of the organ?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Muscle cells**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Muscle cells, also known as muscle fibers, are responsible for the contraction and relaxation that results in the movement of organs and the body.
 
• There are three types of muscle cells: skeletal, cardiac, and smooth muscles, each with specific functions in the body.
 
• Skeletal muscles are attached to bones and are involved in voluntary movements such as walking and lifting.
 
• Cardiac muscles are found in the heart and are responsible for pumping blood throughout the body.
 
• Smooth muscles are found in organs such as the intestines and blood vessels, and they control involuntary movements like the digestion process and regulation of blood flow.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Myofibrils:**

 
 
• Myofibrils are the basic rod-like units of a muscle cell that are composed of repeating sections called sarcomeres, which are the contractile units.
 
• Each myofibril contains thick (myosin) and thin (actin) filaments that slide past each other to produce muscle contraction.
 
 
 
• **Neuromuscular Junction:**
 
 
• The neuromuscular junction is the synapse or connection between a motor neuron and a muscle fiber.
 
• It is where the nervous system communicates with muscles to trigger contraction through the release of neurotransmitters like acetylcholine.
 
 
 
• **ATP and Muscle Contraction:**
 
 
• Adenosine triphosphate (ATP) is the energy currency of the cell, and its hydrolysis provides the energy needed for muscle contraction.
 
• Muscle contraction occurs when ATP binds to myosin, allowing it to interact with actin and produce a power stroke.
 
 
 
• **Muscle Tone:**
 
 
• Muscle tone refers to the continuous and passive partial contraction of muscles, which helps maintain posture and ensures muscles are ready for action.
 
• It is regulated by the nervous system and is essential for maintaining balance and coordinating movements.
